To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the evacuation of a single high-rise building can be performed in less than 20 min using a single occupant evacuation elevator or a combination of transfer floors and a sky-bridge.
the use of occupant elevators and transfer floors are key elements in the design of evacuation strategies for total evacuation in high rise buildings.
the evacuation of high-rise buildings is a complex process and it is strongly affected by the occupants' behaviours, the evacuation strategies and the design of the building.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of egression models to assess the most effective strategy in the case total evacuation of high-rise buildings.
the development of an evacuation model that can provide a quantitative assessment of the effectiveness of different evacuation strategies in high-rise buildings.
the development of a methodology that could be applied to a wide range of buildings to assess the effectiveness of different egress strategies in the case of a total evacuation of the building.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the case of high-rise buildings, the sole use of stairs is not recommended and the sole use of elevators is only recommended in the case of buildings with a small number of occupants.
, in order to obtain the optimal strategy in terms of total evacuation times, it is necessary to take into account the occupants’ behaviour, which should be properly modelled.

, in order to optimise total evacuation strategies for a high-rise building, the sole use of elevators or the combined use of stairs and elevator is not enough and that transfer floors and skybridges are the best egress components to be considered.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of occupant elevators is the preferred strategy for high-rise buildings and that the combined use of sky-bridges and transfer floors is the second preferred strategy.
the use of occupant elevator evacuation is the most effective strategy in high-rise buildings, provided that the elevators are designed to be used by the occupants in case of emergency.
the use of occupant elevators is a key factor in reducing evacuation times.
The main takeaway from our work is that
evacuation times are significantly reduced when occupants are able to move from stairs to elevators or vice versa.
the sole use of stairways is not an appropriate strategy for total evacuation in high rise buildings.
the use of evacuation models can be a powerful tool to help the design and the assessment of total evacuation strategies.
